messages:
mike: Heads-up — EU traffic spiked ~3x on the new v3.5 rollout. Deploy-bot shows elevated 5xxs on inference-proxy EU region. Holding further traffic.
deploy-bot: [automated] rollout paused at 40% traffic (v3.5) due to p95 latency > 750ms for 5m in eu-west-1. Auto-rollback not triggered (threshold 10m). See /deploy/logs/3165554321
tara: Thanks — putting a manual hold. @sagar can you check routing changes? I see KV cache warmup lagging.
sagar: Looking now. KV cache miss rate jumped after the canary shift. Initial hypothesis: a kernel flag in the image increased memory working set for a subset of hosts.
emily: If it's kernel-related we should avoid a full rollback until we confirm impact on latencies vs error type. Can we split traffic back to canary and baseline? :thinking_face:
mike: Yes — prefer partial traffic split to limit customer impact. @deploy-bot can you set traffic: v3.5=10%, v3.4=90% for eu-west-1 and hold? Keep other regions unaffected.
deploy-bot: command accepted: set-traffic --region eu-west-1 --v3.5 10 --v3.4 90
ops-oncall: Executed. Traffic shifted. Monitoring. p95 dropped from 760ms -> 420ms within 90s. 5xxs declining.
tara: Good. Next: do we pin v3.4 for Dedicated customers for now, or do we proceed with a fast rollback for hosted? We need stakeholder comms if we pin.
sagar: Quick check: the problematic hosts are a 12% subset running kernel flag gl-quant-opt. We can roll a hotfix to flip the flag on those hosts and re-evaluate in 30m. That avoids a full revert.
emily: Hotfix timeline looks 20–30m if we can coordinate infra. I recommend drafting a short customer note: "We detected elevated latency in eu-west-1 following a rollout; we've shifted traffic back and are investigating. No data exposure. Some customers may see transient errors." Keep it minimal.
mike: Agreed. @tara can you post to #customer-facing with that template and mention SRE will update in 30m? I'll also update release notes with a note about progressive rollout issues.
tara: On it. Draft:
"We observed increased latency for some requests in eu-west-1 after today's v3.5 deployment. We've reduced traffic to the previous version and are rolling a targeted fix to a subset of hosts. No customer data was impacted. We'll provide updates in 30 minutes."

ops-oncall: Adding runbook link and rollback cmds: https://intranet.redwood/runbooks/deploy-rollback

```# rollback snippet (if needed)
redwoodctl rollout revert --region eu-west-1 --from v3.5 --to v3.4 --reason "latency spike"
redwoodctl set-traffic --region eu-west-1 --v3.5 0 --v3.4 100
```
ops-oncall: If we need to revert, follow the runbook and page SRE lead. Manual approval required for Dedicated rollbacks.
mike: Let's hold on full revert. Proceed with hotfix for gl-quant-opt flag on affected hosts. If errors or p95 doesn't stabilize in 30m, escalate to manual rollback.
sagar: Hotfix rolling now to 25% of affected hosts. I'll post progress every 5m. :rocket:
emily: Thx — I'll monitor customer-facing comms and prepare a brief for sales if key customers ping.
tara: Noted. Adding a release note draft: "v3.5 - rolled back partially in eu-west-1 due to unexpected latency increase; targeted kernel config fix deployed; investigating further". Will finalize after 30m.
mike: Thanks team. Keep thread updates short. If we hit auto-rollback conditions (10m sustained p95>750ms) we will let the bot revert automatically but for now manual hold + hotfix.
sagar: 5m update: hotfix at 25% -> p95 improved on treated hosts. Continuing.
ops-oncall: 15m update: overall eu-west-1 p95 stable at 380ms, 5xxs near baseline. Recommend continue monitoring and keep v3.5 at 10% for 60m.
emily: Recommend we cancel dedicated pin for now; keep canary small and follow up with a post-mortem entry linking this thread.
mike: ok closing plan: maintain v3.5=10% eu-west-1, hotfix rollout complete, monitor 60m, customer note posted. If regression returns escalate to manual revert. :white_check_mark:
